profile.summary: bacformer-for-ppi-prediction is a Bacformer checkpoint whose configuration declares the model class BacformerForProteinProteinInteraction, that is a Bacformer encoder with a head for protein-protein interaction prediction. Bacformer itself treats a whole bacterial genome as a sequence of proteins in genomic order and computes an embedding for each protein that depends on the other proteins in the genome. The published model card for this repository is the automatically generated template and describes neither the training data nor the licence, so most of this page comes from the configuration file, the Hugging Face metadata and the repository README.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Bacformer embeds each protein of a genome with a base protein language model, averages the amino acid embeddings into one vector per protein and runs a transformer over those vectors in genomic order. This checkpoint's configuration declares 12 hidden layers, hidden size 480, 8 attention heads and a maximum of 6000 proteins per genome, and the model class is BacformerForProteinProteinInteraction with a single-label classification head.

quotes.text: Bacformer is a prokaryotic foundational model which models whole-bacterial genomes as a sequence of proteins ordered by their genomic coordinates on the chromosome and plasmid(s).

sections.title: What distinguishes this checkpoint
sections.body: It is the only Bacformer repository read here whose configuration declares a protein-protein interaction model class, and the Hugging Face safetensors index reports 26,802,241 parameters for it. No source explains how this count relates to those of the other Bacformer checkpoints. The preprint reports that Bacformer predicts protein-protein interactions from STRING DB both zero-shot and after finetuning, but it does not name this Hugging Face checkpoint, so the link between the two is not established by the files read here.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Bacformer encoder with a protein-protein interaction head: the configuration declares the class BacformerForProteinProteinInteraction and a single-label classification problem type.

quotes.text: Bacformer is a prokaryotic foundational model which models whole-bacterial genomes as a sequence of proteins ordered by their genomic coordinates on the chromosome and plasmid(s).

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 12 hidden layers, hidden size 480, 8 attention heads, intermediate size 1280, up to 6000 proteins and 1000 contigs per genome, as the configuration file states.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: The proteins of one bacterial genome in genomic order, as average protein embeddings from a protein language model, which is how the README describes Bacformer's input; the configuration allows up to 6000 proteins.

quotes.text: It takes as input average protein embeddings from protein language models and computes contextualised protein embeddings conditional on other proteins present in the genome. Bacformer is trained on a diverse dataset of ~1.3M bacterial genomes and ~3B proteins.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A single-label classification output, as the configuration's problem_type states, over the 100 generic labels the configuration declares (LABEL_0 to LABEL_99), whose meanings no source gives.

gaps: The card says nothing: no training data, no label meanings, no licence for the weights, no evaluation. Everything specific to this checkpoint here comes from the configuration file and the Hugging Face metadata.
The preprint describes a Bacformer model finetuned on STRING protein-protein interaction labels but does not name Hugging Face checkpoints, so this page does not claim the two are the same model.

notes: The weights licence is an open question for this record: the card states none and the Hugging Face API response carries no licence field, while the preprint says the study's models are Apache 2.0. The record's description in the database says the head was trained on STRING DB pair labels; no file read here states that, so it is left out of the page. A reviewer could confirm it from the Bacformer code or by asking the authors.
